previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted for IV antibiotic treatment of resistant E. coli and Prevotella osteomyelitis in the right foot following a recent amputation. He was started on imipenem in the hospital and transitioned to outpatient ertapenem for a four-week course. A PICC line was successfully placed via the right brachial vein under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance to facilitate antibiotic delivery. During the admission, his blood pressure was elevated, prompting an increase in chlorthalidone dose. He remained afebrile with stable labs and no signs of systemic infection. Blood cultures were negative. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue wound care, immunosuppressants, and insulin, and to follow up with primary and infectious disease clinics.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with LUE AVG here with non-healing ulcer over the left index 
finger s/p ligation of AVG.

On HD 1 the patient was admitted to the transplant surgical 
service after evaluation in the ED which revealed pain in his 
hand, typically in the palm and usually at night. He denied any 
systemic signs of infection or illness and the graft had not 
been used since his most recent kidney transplant. He was 
brought to the floor, placed on IVF and made NPO at midnight in 
anticipation of his procedure. In the ED, the patient was 
evaluated by the vascular surgery team with plans to follow up 
as an outpatient after surgical ligation of his LUE AV graft.  

On HD2/POD0, the patient was hyperglycemic with FSBG readings of 
~300-400, and he was hypertensive to a max of 200/100; he 
received hydralazine and re-started his home BP meds which 
normalized his blood pressures.  ___ was consulted for 
insulin sliding scaled recs which were implemented prior to 
discharge. The patient went to the OR and the patient underwent 
ligation of LUE AV graft, which went well without complication 
(reader referred to the Operative Note for details). After a 
brief, uneventful stay in the PACU, the patient arrived on the 
floor on IV fluids and antibiotics, and morphine for pain 
control.  The patient was hemodynamically stable.
The patient was seen by transplant nephrology who continued a 
prior workup for hyperaldosteronism; aldosterone and renin 
levels were sent and will be followed up by that team as an 
outpatient.  

On HD3/POD1, He was started on eplerenone per transplant 
nephrology recs.  The patient was evluated by the plastic 
surgery hand service with no acute recommendations and plans to 
follow up as an outpatient.  
  
At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
with stable vital signs.  The patient was tolerating a regular 
diabetic diet, ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain 
was well controlled.  The patient received discharge teaching 
and follow-up instructions with understanding verbalized and 
agreement with the discharge plan.
